# docs_audit_report — 2026-07-03

## TL;DR (stranger's 30-second take)
The hero is genuinely good — one clear sentence on what Carnot does, a
concrete 47+28 example, and a copy-paste `pip install` — so most strangers
would keep reading past the fold. But trust leaks fast below it: a
"Recent progress" text box is visibly wedged into the headline-stats row,
the license says MIT-0 at the top and Apache 2.0 at the bottom, and the
"Evidence" section is a 12-card wall of insider acronyms and a few
too-perfect numbers. A skeptical stranger keeps reading but leaves unsure
whether to trust the numbers or which license they'd actually be adopting.

## TOP 3 PROBLEMS
1. Contradictory license — hero badge "MIT-0 · Open Source" (line 291) vs
   footer "Apache 2.0 License" (line 766). A stranger cannot tell what
   they'd be adopting.
2. Two broken layouts on first scroll — the "Recent progress" r-card is a
   flex child of the headline stats bar (lines 304–315) so it renders as a
   box jammed next to the four stats; and the 7th "capability" card is
   orphaned outside its grid (grid closes line 494, card is lines 495–501),
   so it renders full-width and off-pattern. Page looks unfinished.
3. Results section is an unverifiable jargon wall — 12 dense cards citing
   undefined acronyms (CCTU, CRANE, VeriCoT, SVAMP, EstimationVerifier,
   PRM-BiasBench, "publication gate") plus suspiciously perfect / impossible
   numbers (1.0, 60/60, "0.125 AUC baseline"). This is the section meant to
   earn trust and it actively erodes it.

## DETAILED FINDINGS

### Bloat
- Results grid (`#results`, lines 517–578) — 12 result cards — a stranger
  skims none of them. Suggested cap: pick the 5–6 strongest headline rows,
  move the rest to the technical report.
- Nav bar (lines 264–277) — 12 text links + 2 buttons — too many entry
  points for a landing page. Suggested cap: ~5 links (Get Started, Results,
  Paper, GitHub, HuggingFace).
- Note: no card is egregiously over the word caps — the "Recent progress"
  card (~52 words), results intro (~50 words), and preprint desc (~88 words)
  are all under their limits. Bloat is NOT this page's main failure mode;
  jargon, layout, and inconsistency are.

### Internal jargon
- Stats bar, line 306 — "382 Completed milestones" — a "milestone" is an
  internal project unit; as a headline vanity metric it means nothing to an
  outsider and reads like self-directed status reporting.
- Recent-progress card, line 312 — "Repinned from v2 0.9857", "5-seed
  dual-condition", "architecture-only 0.8947" — "repinned", "v2", and
  "dual-condition" are insider terms; leading with "our old number was
  wrong" in the hero, in jargon, dents confidence before the reader has any.
- Features card, lines 497–499 — "Test-Time Compute (TTC) & PREM… scales
  TTC based on Process-Reward Energy Model (PREM) variance… intrinsic
  motivation for continuous self-learning" — the single most opaque block on
  the page. Grandiose and says nothing a user can act on.
- Results tags — "CCTU" (451, 574), "CRANE" (554), "VeriCoT" (559),
  "SVAMP / EstimationVerifier" (549), "PRM-BiasBench" (564), "HalluGuard v3"
  (569), "publication gate" (530) — undefined acronyms/benchmarks and an
  internal versioned name; a stranger cannot evaluate any of them.
- Preprint section title, line 584 — "(paper-v6)" — internal version number
  in a public heading; nobody outside the project needs to know it's the 6th
  draft.
- Preprint body, lines 591–594 — "non-operator environment", "operator-
  initiated upload" — "operator" is the project's internal word for the
  maintainer; strangers read it as robotics/telecom and are confused.

### Per-milestone narrative
- Largely avoided (no ".NNN archived …" prose) — good. The residue is the
  milestone-count vanity stat (line 306) and the "Repinned from v2 0.9857"
  version narrative (line 312), both flagged above under jargon.

### Inconsistencies
- License: "MIT-0" (meta line 7, hero badge line 291) vs "Apache 2.0
  License" (footer line 766). Direct contradiction — highest-severity trust
  issue on the page.
- "FoVer" used two incompatible ways: as the headline benchmark where Carnot
  scores 0.9131 (lines 308, 312, 589) AND as a weak baseline scoring "0.125"
  that Carnot beats (line 550). A reader cannot tell if FoVer is the win or
  the strawman.
- Three different ~0.9 AUROC/AUC numbers for three different things —
  0.9131 FoVer (308), 0.91 prompt-injection (530), 0.90 SVAMP (550) — blur
  together on a skim into one vaguely-remembered "0.9 AUROC" claim.
- Worked example flips mid-page: "47 + 28 = 7" (line 338) vs "47 + 28 = 76"
  (lines 329, 343) — the intent (partial vs complete generation) isn't
  signposted, so it reads as a typo.

### Missing essentials
- License clarity — present but self-contradicting (see Inconsistencies).
  This is the one "missing essential" that is actually broken, not absent.
- Everything else a stranger needs is present: one-sentence "what it does"
  (hero, good), install (`pip install carnot-ebm`), maintainer (footer names
  Ian Blenke). "Why trust the numbers" is nominally answered ("backed by a
  checked-in experiment artifact") but undermined by the fabrication signals
  below.

### Fabrication signals
- Line 560 — "GSM8K extraction TP rate: 0.5 → 1.0" — a perfect 1.0 with no
  sample size or credibility anchor on the card.
- Line 565 — "k=5 ensemble catches 60/60 attacks" — perfect 60/60; small-N
  perfection reads as cherry-picked without a false-positive rate beside it.
- Line 550 — "0.90 AUC (vs 0.125 FoVer baseline)" — an AUC of 0.125 is far
  *below* random (0.5); a below-chance baseline looks like an error or a
  rigged comparison, and it's the one card using the purple/"reason" accent,
  hinting it's a different (synthetic?) provenance the card doesn't state.
- The results intro (lines 510–516) pre-emptively defends provenance
  ("synthetic-pilot… rows are labeled by provenance") — defensive hedging
  this specific usually signals the authors know some rows are soft.

### Layout / quality bugs (beyond the two in TOP 3)
- Results `.container` (line 507) is never closed before `</section>` (579);
  the features orphan and the stats-bar card come from similar stray/missing
  `</div>`s (dangling `</div>` at line 314). General structural sloppiness a
  careful reviewer notices in "view source."
- Rust code block uses `<span class="num">` (lines 643, 652) but `.num` is
  not defined in CSS (only kw/fn/str/cm, line 231) — those numbers render
  uncolored. `.r-desc` (line 312) is likewise undefined. Cosmetic.

## WHAT'S WORKING
- The hero does its job: the H1 + subhead state what Carnot does in plain
  English, the 47+28 example makes it concrete, and `pip install carnot-ebm`
  is right there. A stranger understands the product in ~10 seconds.
- "Extract → Check → Repair" (`#how`) is genuinely well-written, jargon-light
  landing-page copy — this is the tone the rest of the page should match.

## RECOMMENDED OPERATOR ACTIONS
1. Fix the license contradiction now — decide MIT-0 vs Apache 2.0 and make
   the footer (line 766) match the hero/meta. This is a one-line legal-
   clarity fix and the single highest-value edit.
2. Move the "Recent progress" card out of the stats bar (lift lines 309–313
   out of `.stats-bar`, close the stray `</div>` at 314) and pull the 7th
   capability card back inside its grid (the stray `</div>` at line 494).
3. Cut the Results section to the 5–6 strongest, self-explanatory rows;
   drop or de-acronym CCTU/CRANE/VeriCoT/SVAMP/PRM-BiasBench and either add a
   sample size beside every perfect score (1.0, 60/60) or remove those rows.
4. Fix or explain the "0.125 FoVer baseline" (below-chance AUC) and stop

5. Rewrite the "TTC & PREM" card in user terms or delete it; drop

   the preprint section.
6. Signpost the "47 + 28 = 7" vs "= 76" example so it doesn't read as a typo.
